Goodbye, leave my apartment now.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'let (them)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Пусть он лучше живёт в гостинице.
examples.trans: Let him stay in a hotel instead.

examples.text: Пусть сам смотрит нашу столицу.
examples.trans: Let him tour our capital on his own.

examples.text: Пускают одного явно, а другого тайно.
examples.trans: They send one openly, and another secretly.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'better', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А ты случайно не слишком торопишься?
examples.trans: Are you not rushing things a bit too much?

examples.text: Прости, пожалуйста, я совсем случайно.
examples.trans: Forgive me, please, it was completely accidental.

examples.text: Лучше бы ты правда была беременна!
examples.trans: It would be better if you really were pregnant!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'lives'.

examples.text: Или тебя здесь что-то держит?
examples.trans: Or is something keeping you here?

examples.text: Нет, меня здесь ничего не держит.
examples.trans: No, nothing is keeping me here.

examples.text: Я скоро уезжаю жить в Париж.
examples.trans: I am leaving soon to live in Paris.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Тебе ещё не надоела серая Москва?
examples.trans: Are you not tired of gray Moscow yet?

examples.text: Может, поедешь со мной в Париж?
examples.trans: Maybe you will go to Paris with me?

examples.text: Я целую тебя впервые за пять лет.
examples.trans: I am kissing you for the first time in five years.

meanings.note: Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common feminine noun meaning 'hotel' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Пусть он лучше живёт в гостинице.
examples.trans: Let him stay in a hotel instead.

examples.text: Билетом ведь в гостинице не расплатишься.
examples.trans: After all, you cannot pay at a hotel with a ticket.

examples.text: Скажите, это ваш гостиничный номер?
examples.trans: Tell me, is this your hotel room?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мотреть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'looks', paired with 'посмотреть'.

examples.text: Причём посмотрела кино совершенно бесплатно.
examples.trans: And watched the movie completely for free.

examples.text: Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Look what I've got.

examples.text: Я смотрю телевизор.
examples.trans: I'm watching TV.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'our', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Пусть сам смотрит нашу столицу.
examples.trans: Let him tour our capital on his own.

examples.text: Настя, неси сюда нашу заначку.
examples.trans: Nastya, bring our secret cash stash here.

examples.text: Надо срочно спасать наш ресторан!
examples.trans: We must urgently save our restaurant!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'толица'). Common feminine noun meaning 'capital city' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Пусть сам смотрит нашу столицу.
examples.trans: Let him tour our capital on his own.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть столица.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always capital city.
